control.name: ON/OFF switch with disabling key
control.description: The paddle switch turns the motor on when moved up and off when moved down. With its yellow key removed the switch is disabled, so the motor cannot start. The machine is first connected to power, then turned on.

off_why.power: the machine is not connected to power ('Connects machine to power, and turns machine ON', p. 26)
off_why.key: 'Removal of yellow key disables switch so motor cannot start' (p. 6)

not_described.why: removing the key while the motor runs: p. 6 says only that without it the motor 'cannot start'
inserting the key with the paddle up: the manual describes the key only as disabling the switch (p. 6)
connecting power with the switch on: the manual connects power first, then turns the machine ON (p. 26)

citations.quote: ON/OFF Switch w/Disabling Key: Turns motor ON when moved up; turns motor OFF when moved down. Removal of yellow key disables switch so motor cannot start.
Switch Type ... Paddle Safety Switch w/Disabling Key
Try to start machine with ON/OFF switch. Machine should not start.
Connects machine to power, and turns machine ON.

control.name: Spindle speed: twelve belt settings
control.description: The spindle runs at one of twelve cited speeds, set by the V-belts while the machine is disconnected from power. Only 790 RPM names its belt positions (B-3); the rest are on a label under the closed belt cover and stay out of the twin (Daniel, 2026-10-24). When the motor stops, the spindle coasts to a stop on its own.

spec.change_refused_why: disconnect the machine first: 'To change spindle speed: 1. DISCONNECT MACHINE FROM POWER!' (p. 30)

stand_ins.run_up_s: stand-in: no source gives how long the motor takes to reach speed; to be replaced by Daniel's timing (decision 0025)
stand_ins.coast_down_s: stand-in: 'Always allow spindle to stop on its own' (p. 14) gives no time; to be replaced by Daniel's timing (decision 0025)
stand_ins.ramps: [INFERENCE] the speed rises and falls in a straight line
stand_ins.direction: [INFERENCE] positive about the joint's axis, down the spindle: clockwise seen from above. The manual does not say
stand_ins.initial_rpm: the setting the twin starts at: 790 RPM, the one setting whose belts are cited (p. 30)

citations.quote: To change spindle speed: 1. DISCONNECT MACHINE FROM POWER!
a belt combination of B-3 creates 790 RPM
Always allow spindle to stop on its own.

citations.locator: 2026-10-30: 'It would be nice to time a stroke on any benchtop. Let's attempt it but prepare the information for a stand in if necessary'; the controls 'accessible in the property panel as well'

control.name: Operator's controls: power, key, switch, speed and downfeed handles
control.description: What an operator does at the T33901, in the manual's order of work (p. 26): choose the speed, connect power, turn the machine on, pull a downfeed handle to drill down to the depth stop, release it so the spring returns the quill, turn the machine off and disconnect it. Two scenarios: a drilling stroke, and the manual's test that the switch does not start the motor without its key.

commands.set: connect or disconnect power, insert or remove the key, move the paddle up or down (pp. 6, 26)
commands.set_speed: choose one of the twelve speeds with the belts, disconnected from power (pp. 9, 30)
commands.pull: pull a downfeed handle down: 'Moves spindle down when pulled down' (p. 7)
commands.release: let go of the handle: 'Spindle automatically returns to top position when released' (p. 7)

spec.release_why: 'Spindle automatically returns to top position when released' (p. 7)

drilling-stroke.description: A 1/2 in deep hole with a 1/4 in twist bit in mild steel, in the manual's order of work (p. 26), down to the depth stop where the photos set it (about 43 mm).

steps.note: p. 29's chart gives 1250 RPM for 13/64-3/8 in twist bits in mild steel; 790 is the fastest of the twelve not above it (p. 9), belts B-3 (p. 30)
the spindle comes up to speed (1 s, a stand-in), and a second more
stand-in: the bit down to the work, 1/2 in above the depth stop, in about 1 s
cutting to the depth stop: 0.004 in/rev for a 1/4 in HSS drill (UF, Table 2; UofT, Table 1.1.2) x 790 RPM = 3.16 in/min
'Spindle automatically returns to top position when released' (p. 7)
the spring returns the quill; v3-v6 rested after 3.4-5.7 s (decision 0024)
'Always allow spindle to stop on its own' (p. 14): 5 s, a stand-in
'turns machine OFF and disconnects it from power' (p. 26)

no-key-no-start.description: The manual's test run (p. 24): with the key removed the switch does not start the motor; with the key in, it does.

steps.note: 'Try to start machine with ON/OFF switch. Machine should not start.' (p. 24)
with the key in, the motor starts (p. 6)
the spindle coasts to a stop (p. 14)

stand_ins.pull to the work: 30.3 mm at 0.03 m/s: a stand-in until Daniel's timing (decision 0025)
stand_ins.hold at depth: 1.0 s: a stand-in until Daniel's timing
stand_ins.live_pull_speed_m_s: 0.03 m/s, the stand-in pull, as the Property panel's starting pull speed
stand_ins.bit and hole: a 1/4 in twist bit in mild steel, 1/2 in deep: the scenario's choice, under UF's 3 drill diameters (0.75 in), so no pecking

issues.message: [INFERENCE] 'Max. Distance From Spindle to Column ... 7 in.' (p. 8) is taken to the column's surface, since the swing is 14 in (p. 8), twice 7 in.
[INFERENCE] A handle's bar is 178 mm long, read from its stud's size, 'STUD-DE M12-1.75 X 178, 15' (p. 50).

Not in the manual or any source reached on 2026-10-22: the handle-to-quill ratio, the head's size and the return spring's force (docs/research/2026-10-22-t33901-handle-ratio-and-figures.md). The spring's tension can be adjusted (p. 40).

The speed chart under the belt cover was not readable in any photo found; only 'a belt combination of B-3 creates 790 RPM' is cited (p. 30). Belt positions are left out of the twin, since the cover is closed (Daniel, 2026-10-24).

Stand-ins: the motor's run-up (1 s) and coast-down (5 s), in straight lines. No source gives them; the manual says only 'Always allow spindle to stop on its own' (p. 14). To be replaced by Daniel's timing on a benchtop drill press (decision 0025). [INFERENCE] The spindle turns clockwise seen from above; the manual does not say.

Stand-ins in the drilling-stroke scenario: the pull to the work (30.3 mm at 0.03 m/s) and the hold at depth (1 s), until Daniel's timing (decision 0025). The cutting feed is cited: 0.004 in/rev for a 1/4 in HSS drill (UF, Table 2; UofT, Table 1.1.2) times 790 RPM. The operator's hand is ideal: it follows its path whatever the spring and the handles push back.

Not described by the manual, so refused in a scenario and done with a note in live use: removing the key while the motor runs, inserting it with the paddle up, and connecting power with the switch on (decision 0025).
